transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-15 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~42 min | Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Alex (Redwood SE), Daniel (Redwood Support); Eva, Marco, Sofia, Liam (BluePeak)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on throughput tuning. Reviewed last 48h pilot data, discussed continuous batching behavior at high QPS, concurrency ceilings, queueing/backpressure, observed p95 latency regressions under burst. Agreed on steady-state test and canary plan.

Topics: pilot results, batching window tuning, max inflight/concurrency targets, queue depth policy, KV-cache warmup, fallback routing, cost implications.

[00:00] Priya: hey everyone thanks for making time, quick roll call?
[00:07] Eva: hi eva here, s-r-e, we saw yesterday's run, had some spikes.
[00:11] Marco: marco, ml eng, ready.
[00:14] Sofia: sofia product.
[00:16] Liam: liam, cto.
[00:18] Alex: alex monroe, se at redwood. daniel support in the background.
[00:24] Priya: cool, agenda — recap, deep-dive on the 2am spike, plan for steady-state run, next steps.

[02:02] Alex: quick context, the pilot is currently on dedicated nodes with 8x A100 equiv, we saw good overall throughput but at burst we hit queueing and p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~620ms, which aligns with continuous batching thresholds kicking in.
[02:30] Marco: yeah that's what we saw, interestingly the batch sizes dropped to single digits during the spike which was unexpected.
[02:39] Alex: that suggests the batching_window is too small relative to request arrival patterns; continuous batching tries to fill batches but if concurrency limit hits the inflight slots it can flush small batches to keep latency, causes inefficiency.
[02:55] Eva: can you explain the concurrency ceiling again? our env is set to max_inflight 32 per GPU, but cpu metrics show saturation earlier.
[03:07] Alex: right, max_inflight is per worker process and we have 4 workers per GPU, so effectively 128 possible inflight tokens but other subsystems—queueing thread, gRPC limits—can bottleneck. the kernel scheduling also has sweet spots for batch sizes 32/64/128 based on model.

[05:10] Marco: we also saw kvcache cold misses on some tails — the p99s corresponded to cache warmup. is there a way to pre-warm?
[05:20] Alex: yes, we can do a warmup pass using representative prompts; Redwood has an optional cache prefill API. also for private installs there's a prefetch script we can run at boot. note transcripts may show 'kv cash' in export cause speech rec.

[06:50] Sofia: question — if we increase batch_max to 128, what's the impact on tail latency for small requests?
[06:58] Alex: two effects: batching increases throughput and amortizes decode cost, but if batching_window is large and traffic is sparse you add wait time. we want batch_max 128 with batching_window 10–20ms and concurrency target that allows multiple full-size batches in flight to keep p95 low.

[08:30] Liam: cost — does bigger batches always lower cost?
[08:35] Alex: generally yes cost-per-token drops, but if you add queueing delays and need extra headroom (more GPUs) during peaks cost can go up. there's a sweet spot we try to find — we did analysis vs your workload and 24 concurrency per GPU looked promising.

[10:10] Priya: quick review of yesterday's run: steady 450 rps for 20m, then a burst to 1.8k rps for 90s; during the burst p50 stayed near baseline but p95 spiked.
[10:26] Eva: we replayed traffic and saw the same; logs attached in the shared drive — file name bluepeak_09014_run.csv (note: filename was mis-ocr'd in transcript).

[12:00] Alex: hypotheses — 1) burst causes many short requests that don't fill batches; 2) concurrency global limit tripped and forced many small flushes; 3) KV cache misses for some prompt variants.

[13:05] Marco: can you run a controlled test with steady-state for 10 minutes at 900 rps? we want to see stabilized batch sizes.
[13:12] Alex: yes, plan is to run 10m steady-state at three QPS points: 450, 900, 1400 with settings: concurrency=24, batch_max=128, batching_window=15ms; we'll collect p50/p95/p99, batch size dist, GPU util and queue depth.

[15:00] Daniel: adding: we'll enable the adaptive backpressure metric so we can see queue drops; also will toggle the 'prefer-immediate' policy to measure cost-latency tradeoff.

[17:45] Eva: about prefer-immediate — that was on, might explain why batches were flushed early. we had it set to true to prioritize latency.
[17:52] Alex: okay so for the steady-state we'll flip it to false for one run (allow short hold to fill batches) and true for another. that will show delta.

[20:05] Marco: any concerns about cold-starts when we increase batch_max?
[20:12] Alex: cold starts mainly affect first few requests after model load; batch_max doesn't increase cold-start time but larger batches can hide jitter. pre-warming kvcache and keeping a low-level warm replica helps.

[21:40] Sofia: can we get a simple recommended config for production SLO: p95 < 300ms and cost within 10% of current?
[21:48] Alex: recommended initial config: batch_max=128, batching_window=15ms, concurrency_target=24 per GPU, prefer_immediate=false (for throughput critical), enable kvcache prefill on startup, and scale policy: add 1 GPU at 70% sustained util. we'll measure and adjust.

[24:10] Liam: what about routing fallback — if Dedicated saturates do we failover to hosted smaller model?
[24:20] Priya: yes we can set policy to route overflow to a cheaper variant; we'll provide a routing playbook, including blackhole thresholds and canary percentage.

[26:00] Marco: will changing concurrency to 24 cause memory pressure? our model is 7B quantized, about 20GB per model.
[26:10] Alex: at 24 concurrency we keep memory headroom but need to monitor decode mem for kvcache; we'll include memory utilization charts in the test results.

[28:30] Eva: ok so timeline — when can you run the steady-state?
[28:35] Alex: we can run tonight at 22:00 UTC (or 15:00 PDT) — but need your logs and confirm traffic shaping.
[28:45] Eva: we'll provide the one-hour representative logs by EOD.

[30:00] Priya: recap of agreed test matrix and owners. Alex to run three steady-state runs and share csv + dashboards, Priya to send pricing delta, Eva to upload logs, Marco to confirm prompt distribution.

[32:15] Marco: small nit — we saw some transcripts show 'k v cash' and 'batching wind' in exported fireflies notes, minor.
[32:22] Daniel: yep auto-transcribe quirks.

[34:40] Sofia: for the canary after tests, what's the rollback plan?
[34:47] Alex: automatic fallback to previous routing policy if p95 > 600ms or error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, plus immediate traffic cutover script. we'll send runbook.

[36:50] Liam: curious about cost estimate for using larger batch_max but heavier queueing — can you model that?
[36:57] Priya: we'll provide a short model comparing cost-per-token at current vs tuned config and a scenario with added GPUs for headroom.

[38:30] Eva: last question: is there any reason not to enable the prefill API for kvcache in production?
[38:36] Alex: only consideration is data sensitivity during prefill if items are customer prompts; for your private deployment you control keys and data residency — so it's ok. for hosted we have policies.

[40:00] Priya: ok let's wrap — action items listed in the notes. next sync Friday if tests look good, otherwise we'll reconvene after results. thanks all.
[40:12] Eva: thanks.
[40:15] Marco: thanks team.

End of transcript.
